Audit hooks cannot run scripts, modify arguments, grant approval or retry tools.

Provider is a callable receiving a context and returning {final, calls}.
Session history is context only: resuming never executes recorded calls.
jarvis\\agent_tools.py: Read-only development tools and controlled batches for the shared registry.
jarvis\\anticipation.py:
Evidence-bound idle preparation, independent of the desktop action executor.

Research inspiration: THUNLP ProactiveAgent and AgentACE-AI ProAct. This is an
independent local implementation, not either upstream runtime or benchmark.
jarvis\\anticipation_worker.py: One-shot bounded read-only preparation. No desktop or account tool imports.
jarvis\\application_discovery.py: Read-only adapter to existing app configuration and Windows UI transport.
jarvis\\approval_receipt.py:
Identity of an exact approval request (Prompt 31: P31-001 callback binding, P31-002 receipt replay).

Protocol, shared by every requester and the island card:
1. The requester creates an unpredictable one-time request id *before* enqueueing the card, keeps its own
   copy and its own issue time, and sends the id inside the answer object.
2. The card reads the id once when it is created and digests kind, detail and id; the digest is written to
   the answer only when that card is approved (cards also refuse decisions after APPROVAL_TTL).
3. The requester accepts only ``receipt_valid``: approved, digest equal to the digest of *its* kind, detail
   and locally held id, within its own TTL, and not cancelled. A receipt from an earlier decision, even for a
   request with identical text, carries another id and is refused; each request is answered once.
jarvis\\app_adapters.py:
API/code-first application adapters registered in the existing ToolRegistry.

Each adapter is one execution *method* (see execution_strategy.METHODS):
  office_xlsx / office_docx  openpyxl / python-docx in the separate .venv-skills
  pdf_document               pypdf in the main environment (new outputs only)
  office_automation          a new hidden Excel/Word instance (native object model)
  blender_task               fixed bpy templates in background Blender
  unreal_task                engine Build.version manifest (read-only)
  vscode_cli                 VS Code command-line interface

Writes are transactional: features the method cannot preserve are refused
before input; the edit goes to a temporary copy; an independent process reads it
back; the original is backed up; then one atomic replace commits it. Writes need
runtime approval and leave TaskState checkpoints. Nothing here retries a write.
jarvis\\app_knowledge.py:
What Jarvis knows about the apps on this PC: what each does, its main features, and the buttons it has.

Three layers:
- PROFILES: hand-written knowledge for the apps installed here (built from the 333 Start-menu apps in
  config "apps"): what the app does, its features, and the one question Jarvis offers when you're in it.
- inventory(): every configured app, matched to a profile or given a category from its name and executable.
- AppKnowledge: buttons, menus and tabs learned live through Windows UI Automation each time an app is in
  front (names only: never field values, list contents, chats, passwords or coordinates), saved to
  .jarvis-runtime/app_knowledge.json so Jarvis gets to know an app better the more you use it.
jarvis\\audio.py:
Continuous capture, Silero speech detection, and independent CUDA decoding.

Whisper is chunk based. Rolling hypotheses update once a second; superseded
partials are coalesced while final segments and window boundaries are ordered.
jarvis\\azr_dataset.py:
Versioned, de-duplicated AZR task datasets with leak-proof train/validation/held-out splits.

* Splits are fixed by **disjoint seed ranges and disjoint structure signatures**: a structure skeleton
  (tool sequence or program family + constant) that appears in one split never appears in another,
  so near-duplicates cannot leak between training and evaluation.
* Exact duplicates are removed by task id (content hash); near-duplicates by signature.
* Every record carries provenance: generator, seed, environment/oracle versions, and how its answer
  was obtained (always the deterministic environment or a Jarvis-authored oracle program, never a model).
* Model answers and their verification are stored next to the tasks; incorrect answers are kept for
  analysis but are never written back as ground truth.
jarvis\\azr_proposer.py:
AZR-style proposer with learnability scoring, using local models only (Pillar D).

The proposer (default local ``qwen3.5:9b``) writes a *task*, never an answer: a deduction scenario
(initial state + calls) or an induction program with inputs. The independent oracle then validates
it and computes the answer: the simulation executes calls; induction programs are statically
screened and executed twice in the sandbox (AZR integrity, safety and determinism checks).
Learnability follows AZR: r_propose = 1 - mean solve rate over G solver rollouts, and 0 when
the task is never or always solved. Proposals that fail validation receive the AZR format
penalty (-1) and are kept only in the rejection log, never in a dataset.
jarvis\\azr_reward.py:
Independent verifiable rewards for AZR answers (Pillar D, Part C).

Rewards are computed only from the oracle: the deterministic simulation (deduction, abduction)
and sandboxed execution (induction). The reward code never imports or reads candidate training
outputs other than the answer text it scores. AZR's composite reward is used:
correct = 1, well-formatted but wrong = -0.5, format/safety failure = -1.
Induction also reports visible-only passes, so memorising the shown examples cannot score as
generalisation, and repeatability (every case is executed twice).
jarvis\\azr_sandbox.py:
Restricted execution of induction answers (model-written Python) for the AZR oracle.

Model code is never executed in the Jarvis process. Each batch runs in the reviewed MCP runtime
container (no network, read-only root, no capabilities, non-root, PID/memory/CPU limits and a
lifetime fence; see ``mcp_synthesis.server_config``) behind a Jarvis-owned harness. The harness
forks one child per program with restricted builtins and OS limits (CPU seconds, address space,
no core files) and kills it after a wall-clock deadline, so a runaway C-level loop or allocation
loses only that program. Every case is run twice so nondeterministic programs fail (AZR's
determinism check). The static screen (``azr_tasks.screen_program``) runs first; passing it is not
treated as proof of safety.
jarvis\\azr_tasks.py:
Absolute Zero-style synthetic reasoning tasks over a disposable computer state (Pillar D).

Adapted from the method of Absolute Zero (LeapLabTHU/Absolute-Zero-Reasoner, MIT; arXiv 2505.03335):
tasks come in three modes and every answer is judged by execution, never by a model:

* DEDUCTION  given an initial state and a tool-call sequence, predict the exact final state
             (trains state-transition prediction for ``cognition.predict``);
* ABDUCTION  given an initial and a desired state, produce a dependency-respecting tool-call DAG
             that reaches it (trains planning/tool selection for ``brain.py``); any DAG whose every
             valid execution order reaches the desired state is correct;
* INDUCTION  given visible input/output examples, write a Python function that also passes hidden
             cases (trains small capability generation for ``repo_abilities``).

The environment is a pure, in-memory simulation: no real file, window or clipboard is touched.
No AZR code is copied; the AZR executor is described upstream as research-only and is not used.

jarvis\\capabilities.py: Local intent routing over the real registry; reference data never adds handlers.

What Jarvis can do, which APIs it is connected to, and when to use what.

Answers are built from Jarvis's own registries and the latest live API check, so they stay accurate when
features change. "check your APIs" runs that live check (about 30 seconds) and saves the result.
jarvis\\catalog.py: Exact, ambiguity-aware name lookup for the local path catalog.
jarvis\\clarification.py: Explicit task questions and conservative matching of short option replies.
jarvis\\claude_code.py: Local-only Claude Code CLI coding runner with island progress and owned Stop.
jarvis\\claude_code_guard.py: Claude Code source boundary validation; never grants shell permission.
jarvis\\claude_code_permissions.py: Local stdio MCP permission handler for the owned Claude Code session.
jarvis\\claude_code_proxy.py:
Task-owned loopback Anthropic adapter; local model only, thinking disabled.

Claude Code omits rather than disables third-party thinking. Qwen defaults to
thinking, so make the supported Ollama Messages API control explicit. The CLI
and this server share one Windows job; no daemon, restart or request replay.
jarvis\\cloud_architect.py:
Optional, sanitized cloud "algorithm architect" consultation after repeated local reasoning failure.

Disabled by default. Local Qwen remains the executor; the cloud model only returns
advice for a *generic* problem rebuilt from public facts or synthetic examples.

Eligibility (all required): the feature and the Groq provider are enabled on a
confirmed free account (never a paid upgrade); the user authorized cloud
consultation for this request or a named policy scope; the problem is complex
algorithmic/coding/planning work with three distinct, verified local strategy
failures caused by insufficient reasoning (not credentials, denial, unsafe actions
or outages); the automatic planning budget (five attempts) is not exceeded by the
consultation; quota is available; and the payload passes the privacy gate.

Privacy gate: classify provenance, build the generic problem, strip paths,
filenames, usernames, emails, tokens, source snippets, logs and internal names,
reject if sensitive semantics remain, validate the payload against an explicit
allowlist, and default to local whenever any check is inconclusive. Redaction is not
a privacy guarantee; this gate refuses rather than trusting it. Local telemetry stores
only categorical decisions, payload size/digest and opaque correlation, never the payload.

Cloud output is untrusted text. It never receives tools, files or commands. Code in
the advice is statically screened and executed only against the problem's own
examples inside the network-less container sandbox (Phase 3 runtime); only then may
it be proposed to the skill engine as a provisional CAPTURED candidate.
jarvis\\cloud_cli.py: Local cloud controls; live smoke requires two explicit opt-ins and free gating.
jarvis\\cloud_policy.py: Deterministic, fail-closed public question policy. No model or network calls.
jarvis\\cloud_quota.py: Cross-process SQLite reservations; conservative rolling windows, no LLM counting.
jarvis\\coder.py: Small, project-scoped coding tasks with checked model output and atomic writes.
jarvis\\codex_browser_check.py: Owned local browser interaction check, executed by the validation worker.
jarvis\\codex_code.py: Isolated local Codex/Qwen coding sessions with owned Stop and island streams.
jarvis\\codex_files.py: Owned Codex stdio MCP source tools: checked reads, backups and exact edits.
jarvis\\codex_proxy.py: Task-owned Responses relay to local Ollama; bounded source tools only.
jarvis\\codex_validation.py: Expected deliverables, independent checks and fresh-source repair packets.
jarvis\\codex_workload.py:

No operator credentials, server changes, remote pushes, or main-branch merges.
All mutations are checkpointed once; interrupted runs are retained for inspection.
jarvis\\code_context.py:
Read-only project discovery inspired by agenticSeek's file-finder workflow.

Independently implemented for Jarvis; no upstream source is imported or executed.
jarvis\\code_stream.py: Decode streamed JSON source and keep guarded, visible coding drafts.
jarvis\\coding_activity.py: Actual coding activity and review events; display failures never replay work.
jarvis\\coding_console.py: Bounded native coding activity with inspectable commands and real source diffs.
jarvis\\coding_curriculum.py:
100 distinct JSON CLI projects, with independent executable reference cases.

Reference expressions below are developer-authored, never model-generated.
They are used only by the evaluator and are not supplied to the coding model.
jarvis\\coding_files.py: Native workspace tools using Jarvis's checked, non-replaying save boundary.
jarvis\\coding_languages.py: Bounded, first-party language guidance. No model commands are executed here.
jarvis\\coding_lessons.py: Verified coding experience, not executable plans or model weight changes.
jarvis\\coding_operations.py: Typed equivalents of the command reference, inside checked source scope.
jarvis\\coding_processes.py: Owned command sessions, bounded polling and actual console activity.
jarvis\\coding_programs.py: Discover real local coding programs; never installs or borrows credentials.
jarvis\\coding_training_data.py:
Build reference-derived corrections from the trusted local curriculum oracle.

Never processes model-generated expressions or code. Executable case checks here

jarvis\\cognition.py:
Jarvis's cognitive architecture: one continuous perceive -> remember -> reason -> decide -> act -> learn loop.

The six modules match the architecture diagram (Multimodal Perception, Working Memory, Long-Term Memory, Core
Reasoning & World Model, Executive Control & Meta-Learning, Action / Tool Output). They are wired around the
subsystems Jarvis already has rather than replacing them:

- Perception: speech and typed commands, the focused window (vision), background sensors (God's Eye, weather,
  WhatsApp, repository browsing) and feedback from every action. Each percept gets a salience score.
- Working memory: a bounded workspace (goal, focus, active task, pending decisions, session style and seven
  attention slots) that every answer and task plan sees through context_hub.situation().
- Long-term memory: one recall interface over episodic memory (conversation summaries, Obsidian activity),
  declarative memory (curated facts) and procedural memory (skill and experience memory, coding lessons, learned
  repositories, plus the per-action outcome statistics kept here).
- World model: before an action runs it predicts the effects, whether they are reversible or external, whether
  approval is needed, the expected time and the chance of success, and lists what it is uncertain about.
- Executive control: proceeds, or asks when a consequential action rests on an unresolved reference. After the
  action it compares outcome with prediction, learns timing and reliability, treats corrections ("no, that's
  wrong") as negative feedback, and consolidates lessons into the Obsidian vault.
- Action: Actions.execute; its result flows back into perception, closing the loop.

Nothing here sends, types or clicks by itself: it observes, predicts, asks and learns.
jarvis\\command_cleanup.py: Local proposal-only speech cleanup; finite edits, never inferred intent.
jarvis\\command_reference.py: User-supplied command reference as data, with native usage and approval routing.
jarvis\\config_contract.py: Shallow startup contract. Unknown fields warn without granting new permissions.
jarvis\\context_hub.py:
One snapshot of everything going on, so Jarvis can keep several contexts in mind at once.

Each question and task plan gets a compact "situation": what is on screen, which repository you are looking at
(and whether Jarvis has learned it), the task running and the queue, questions Jarvis is waiting on, what is
playing, the active project, recent conversation topics, and background learning. Jarvis can then answer
"what is this repo about?", "go back to the email thing" or "is that done yet?" without being told which context
you mean. Everything here is cheap to read (no network, no model) and bounded in size.
jarvis\\context_selector.py: One bounded, daemon context-selection thread; no tools or task execution.
jarvis\\conversation_intent.py:
Natural conversation phrasing: openers, video/music wording and chat-vs-task routing.

Spoken requests such as "let's make an email" or "let's watch a video on YouTube"
become the commands Jarvis already understands. Utterances no rule recognises are
classified as conversation or a task before any planning happens, so ordinary talk
("I'm tired today") gets a reply instead of a desktop task.
jarvis\\conversation_memory.py: Paired, durable sessions and bounded context projections; no action execution.
jarvis\\dag_execution.py:
Bounded task-scoped DAG scheduling over existing synchronous tool adapters.

Thread workers fit Jarvis's existing transports. A deadline requests cooperative
cancellation; workers are drained before returning, never abandoned or replayed.
jarvis\\deerflow.py: Owned, bounded DeerFlow inference/research process; Jarvis keeps execution policy.
jarvis\\deerflow_cli.py: Run the real DeerFlow harness on one scoped Jarvis source-research question.
jarvis\\deerflow_media.py: Literal-spec free media creation; no API, host execution or account writes.
jarvis\\deerflow_media_runner.py: Trusted, keyless media recipes; invoked only in the offline Docker job.
jarvis\\deerflow_model.py:
LangChain model using Jarvis's real local Qwen prompt-format/GPU admission code.

Imported only by the isolated Python 3.12 DeerFlow worker.
jarvis\\deerflow_sandbox.py: Offline, resource-limited Docker workspace. Effects are never auto-replayed.
jarvis\\deerflow_worker.py: One-shot embedded upstream DeerFlow. Only Jarvis's scoped reads are offered.
jarvis\\deliberation.py:
Jarvis's deliberation layer: independent reasoning, opinions and decisions.

A single shared decision engine wired at the central task choke point, rather than a
separate feature or a duplicated loop. For a non-trivial task it forms an evidence-based
opinion over the user's existing systems (cognition memory/reliability, skills, capability
routing), classifies risk, estimates confidence, and decides whether to simply proceed,
voice a brief recommendation, or propose-and-wait. It interprets conversational feedback
("go ahead" / "no, try something else" / "you decide") and keeps a traceable decision
ledger whose outcomes are fed back from the cognition loop.

Design constraints honoured here:
- Never blocks a turn: every model call is bounded and falls back to a heuristic opinion.
- Never fabricates confidence or memory: model claims are typed (fact/assumption/
  prediction/preference); unknown preferences are not asserted as fact.
- Never expands authority: high-risk actions still funnel through the existing single
  approval path; this layer advises and sequences, it does not grant permissions.
- "Speak up only when it matters": stays silent on simple/agreed low-risk work.
jarvis\\demonstration.py:
Show Me Once: learn one identifiable UI action from an explicit, consented user demonstration.

Flow: Jarvis asks (spoken through F5) for a single demonstration in a selected window;
recording starts only after explicit consent, scoped to that window's process; a
low-level mouse hook observes clicks. Injected input -- including Jarvis's own cyan
cursor, which uses Windows touch injection -- is never treated as the user's.
For each user click inside the scoped window the recorder captures the UI Automation
element (control type, AutomationId, accessible name, class, ancestry) and the
observed before/after state; relative coordinates are kept only as a last-resort
fallback. Transient RuntimeIds, keyboard input, field values and anything inside a
password field are never stored.

A demonstration becomes a minimal provisional skill only after Jarvis replays the
selector through the structured UIA path in a safe context and observes the same
postcondition. Trust then follows the Phase 3 lifecycle (independent verified use).
jarvis\\desktop_actions.py: Validated UIA operations shared by direct commands and planned steps.
jarvis\\desktop_tasks.py: Bounded Windows tasks that require an actual named window or folder.
jarvis\\development.py: Jarvis's staged web/app workflow, backed by real project tooling.
jarvis\\development_api.py: Planner-facing development tools with explicit scope and human feedback.
jarvis\\development_browser.py: Isolated real Chromium inspection of one owned loopback development preview.
jarvis\\development_design.py: Explicit design brief and reference reasons, before implementation.
jarvis\\development_knowledge.py: Small first-party guides selected by stack; reference data, never permissions.
jarvis\\development_learning.py: Framework-scoped cases from independent build/browser evidence, not weights.
jarvis\\development_native.py: Explicit native packaging/build adapters; no inference-controlled shell.
jarvis\\development_projects.py: Bounded project scaffolds and stages. No package hooks or arbitrary shell.
jarvis\\development_tools.py: Owned, cancellable Node commands and preview. Never replays uncertain commands.
jarvis\\diagnostics.py: Read-only configured service checks; no model loads, repair or task replay.
jarvis\\direct_execution.py: Exact desktop requests bypass inference; unknown intents return to the planner.
jarvis\\display.py: Native Windows DPI setup before Tk creates any windows.
jarvis\\docker_runtime.py: Hidden Docker availability recovery; never owns or stops the shared engine.
jarvis\\documents.py:
Files dropped on Jarvis: read them, index them, answer questions about them, and remember them.

Two indexing modes, chosen by size and context:

* **light** (LightRAG-style): chunks ranked with BM25 plus a keyword/entity co-occurrence graph built without a
  model. Used for small documents (under ``graph_threshold`` characters, about 15 pages) with few named entities.
  Ready in about a second.
* **graph** (GraphRAG-style): the light index first, so questions work at once, then the local model extracts
  entities and relations chunk by chunk in the background and merges them into a knowledge graph. Used for longer
  documents or ones dense with names (people, companies, places).

Questions are answered from the best chunks plus the graph neighbourhood of the entities they mention, with page
citations. Both modes are Jarvis's own local implementations of those approaches (no embedding model is installed on
this PC, so ranking is lexical); they are not the upstream LightRAG or GraphRAG libraries.

Memory: a document lives in the session (with a crash-safe spill under ``.jarvis-runtime/documents/session``). When
the session ends ("done with the pdf", or Jarvis closes), it is saved for good: the index under
``.jarvis-runtime/documents/<id>/`` and a note in the Obsidian vault's ``Jarvis Documents``. The same file dropped
again, or a later question naming it, reconnects to it.
jarvis\\document_worker.py:
One-shot structured document worker (XLSX/DOCX in .venv-skills, PDF in .venv).

Reads one bounded JSON request on stdin and prints one JSON reply. It never
replaces the user's file: writes go to the host-chosen temporary output, which
the host verifies independently before an atomic commit. Not a security sandbox;
it only parses documents with maintained libraries (openpyxl, python-docx, pypdf).
jarvis\\engine.py:
Incremental command boundaries for spoken commands.

Partial hypotheses may change. Only complete clauses separated by 'then' are
committed early; most commands wait for a final ASR segment. There is no
dictation mode: "write ..." is one command (composed or exact text), and
free speech is typed only while the push-to-write keys are held.
jarvis\\everyday_runtime.py: Small, live-data and computed answers; no stored changing answers.
jarvis\\evolution_archive.py:
Darwin Gödel Machine-style evolutionary archive for Jarvis candidates (Pillar C).

Adapted from the method of the Darwin Gödel Machine (jennyzzt/dgm, Apache-2.0; arXiv 2505.22954):
an open-ended archive keeps every evaluated variant with its lineage, and parents are drawn
with probability proportional to a sigmoid of their score times 1/(1 + children), so strong
but under-explored variants are preferred while weaker ones keep a chance (DGM's
``score_child_prop``). DGM checkpoints the archive per generation in ``dgm_metadata.jsonl``;
here a SQLite archive records each candidate and each experiment stage instead. No DGM code
is copied. Differences: candidates are bounded surface mutations (not free-form agent code),
fitness is multi-objective with a Pareto front, and nothing in the archive deploys anything.
jarvis\\evolution_lab.py:
Isolated experiment repository for evolution candidates (Pillar C).

The canonical Jarvis repository is only *read*: ``git rev-parse`` identifies it and its HEAD,
and ``git archive`` exports a snapshot. No branch, worktree, ref or file is created in it.
Experiments live in a separate Git repository under ``.jarvis-runtime/evolution/lab/repo``:
the snapshot is committed there, each candidate is a commit on its own lab branch
``cand/<id>`` built from its parent's lab commit, and evaluation uses detached lab worktrees
that are removed afterwards. The evaluator directory and held-out data are excluded from
snapshots, so candidates can neither read nor modify them.

The lab is not a hostile-code sandbox. Safety comes from what a candidate may be: a change
to one declared surface literal, verified on source text before anything runs.
jarvis\\evolution_promotion.py:
Promotion of qualified evolution candidates: proposal, approval, staged deploy, rollback.

A candidate that passed the sealed retention gate is only a *proposal*. Deploying it needs:
an explicit Dynamic Island approval card (``Actions._approve``), an unchanged evaluator seal,
a production tree still at the candidate's source commit with the surface at its approved
baseline values, a known-good release snapshot, and staged health checks (import readback,
target-domain tests, privacy/security tests). Any failed check restores the snapshot
automatically. Rollback is independent of Jarvis running:

    python -m jarvis.evolution_promotion releases
    python -m jarvis.evolution_promotion rollback <release_id>
jarvis\\evolution_surfaces.py:
Bounded mutation surfaces for controlled self-evolution (Pillar C).

A surface is one module-level dict literal of tunable numbers or strings in a named
Jarvis source file. A candidate may change only the values of that literal, within
declared bounds; every other byte of the module's syntax tree must stay identical.
That rule is checked on source text with ``ast`` and never by importing candidate code.

Security policy, the evaluator, approval authority, deployment controls, tests and
configuration are not surfaces and cannot be targeted (``PROTECTED``).
jarvis\\execution_adapters.py:
Reviewed upstream execution primitives, adapted to Jarvis's existing worker.

Source revisions, licenses and modifications: integrations/execution-primitives/.
These are small ports/adaptations, not installations of the five agent frameworks.
All preparation is read-only. A prepared callback may be dispatched exactly once.
jarvis\\execution_contracts.py:
Shared, metadata-only contracts for execution outcomes (upgrade phases 2-4).

Outcome rows extend the existing agent lifecycle log (agent_events.py); they are
not a second registry or event bus. Every field is categorical or bounded, so a
row never carries arguments, responses, file contents or credentials. A row
describes what independent verification observed; it never grants approval,
selects a tool or authorizes a retry.
jarvis\\execution_router.py: Ordered preflight fallback; one external action, followed by observations only.
jarvis\\execution_strategy.py:
API/code-first execution strategy over the existing ToolRegistry.

Policy: API/code first -> structured automation (DOM/UIA, native object model)
-> GUI coordinates last, but only among methods that are discovered, compatible,
available and authorized for this request. Ranking blends the tier prior with
measured verified outcomes from the shared agent event log (execution_contracts),
verification strength, latency and resource cost. Measured evidence can reorder
or demote methods; it can never make an ineligible or unauthorized method run.

The engine never dispatches by itself: every attempt is a ToolRegistry.execute
call, so scope, deny policy and runtime approval still apply. A fallback is taken
only when the previous method was provably not dispatched (ToolUnavailable is
raised before any input) or the operation is read-only. A dispatched write with an
uncertain outcome stops the plan and is never replayed on another method. GUI
methods are recommended to the planner, which must work from a fresh observation.
jarvis\\experience.py: Local, read-only recall helpers. Memories are evidence, never action queues.
jarvis\\experience_memory.py: Bounded local case-based learning inspired by Memento; no actions or weight updates.
jarvis\\exploration.py:
SEAgent-inspired autonomous exploration curriculum, restricted to verified-isolated environments.

Design reference: SunzeY/SEAgent (commit c8887f15; README states code Apache-2.0,
data CC BY-NC 4.0, research use). No SEAgent code is used: this is an original
curriculum loop -- observe -> propose a small measurable goal -> plan permitted
actions -> execute in the sandbox -> observe the difference -> verify
independently -> record the trajectory -> learn (ReasoningBank lessons, Pillar A
CAPTURED/FIX candidates) -> choose the next goal.

Isolation policy: only environments that are genuinely separated from the user's
session may run. The cyan cursor and Windows virtual desktops are NOT sandboxes, so
desktop GUI exploration stays disabled unless a verified VM backend exists (none
is implemented). Supported environments:
  * IsolatedBrowserEnv: headless Chrome, fresh context (no profile/cookies/downloads),
    every request outside one approved origin aborted.
  * BlenderSandboxEnv: background Blender through ToolRegistry `blender_task` in a
    disposable folder (factory settings, scripts disabled).
Exploration never sends uncertain steps twice: a crash leaves the step marked
uncertain and the next run re-observes a fresh sandbox.
jarvis\\f5_speech.py: F5-TTS adapter for the owned, cancellable continuous audio worker.
jarvis\\fast_workflows.py: Direct navigation/media workflows with fresh checks, without model inference.
jarvis\\file_drop.py:
Drop a file on the island: Pip eats it, then asks what to do with it.

Ask questions about it (indexed LightRAG- or GraphRAG-style by documents.py, then questions go to it for the session),
send it on WhatsApp (to whom, with an optional typed or dictated message, previewed before sending), or send it by
email (recipient or none, body written from what you say, saved as a Gmail draft with the file attached).

Windows reports dropped files with WM_DROPFILES; DropTarget subclasses the island's windows to receive it. The flow
runs on its own thread (one at a time), so a long task never delays it, and every question is answered by clicking
the island, speaking, or typing in the island's answer box.
jarvis\\firecrawl_tools.py: Optional public Firecrawl v2 reads using a separately configured Jarvis key.
jarvis\\folder_lookup.py: Drive-scoped folder discovery and local preferences for opening folders.
jarvis\\glass_ui.py: Native rounded glass controls. Shared artwork drives Tk and rendered previews.
jarvis\\gmail_api.py: Local OAuth Gmail REST adapter: read, draft, send, trash and labels. No automatic replay of mailbox writes.
jarvis\\gmail_bridge.py: Bounded local extension transport. Leased actions are never dispatched twice.
jarvis\\gmail_chrome_worker.py:
Named-control Gmail operations in the user's existing Chrome session.

No profile copying, password extraction, SMTP login or physical mouse movement.
jarvis\\gmail_workflows.py:
API-first Gmail command workflows: read, speak, draft, send, trash and labels.

Every mailbox write is approved once, verified by readback and never replayed.
jarvis\\gmail_writes.py: Durable no-replay guards for approved mailbox writes; no message text stored.
jarvis\\gods_eye.py:
God's Eye View, fully wired into Jarvis.

* Server: the local God's Eye View app (integrations/gods-eye-view-src) starts with Jarvis and is kept running.
* Visualization: "show me Paris", "show flights near me", "show military over the Gulf", "what's the weather
  doing", "show traffic cameras in London", "switch to thermal" open God's Eye in Jarvis's browser and drive it

* Runtime absorption: a side thread polls the God's Eye server every minute for a 25-mile (40 km) radius around

  questions ("why is it so loud outside?", "why am I hearing sirens?") before any web search, the multi-context
  situation, and proactive alerts on the island.
jarvis\\gods_eye_cameras.py:
Extra live traffic cameras for God's Eye View: Toronto (keyless) and Ontario 511 (with your free key).

God's Eye ships camera packs for London, Austin, Calgary, British Columbia, Finland, Norway and a few others.
Its own Ontario 511 pack stopped working when 511on.ca started requiring a developer key for its camera list,
which left Toronto, Mississauga and Brampton empty. This module builds a camera pack God's Eye already knows
how to read (CCTV_SOURCES_FILE) from:

- City of Toronto open data: 336 intersection cameras, refreshed every few minutes, no key.
- Ontario 511's official API, when you save a free developer key in secrets/ontario511.json
  ({"api_key": "..."}) or the ONTARIO_511_API_KEY environment variable. That adds the 400-series highway
  cameras through Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton and the rest of Ontario.

The pack lives under .jarvis-runtime (outside God's Eye's source, so "update God's Eye" keeps it) and God's Eye's
own .env points at it. Live packs stay on (CCTV_FORCE_AUSTIN=1), so nothing God's Eye already shows is lost.
jarvis\\gods_eye_update.py:
Update the local God's Eye View checkout from upstream without losing local state.

The current folder is kept as a dated backup (source only), the newest upstream main is unpacked in its place,
and `node_modules`, `.env`, caches and logs are moved across. `npm ci` runs only when the lockfile changed.
jarvis\\gods_eye_view.py: On-demand launcher for Bilawal Sidhu's local God's Eye View console.

Process-shared, priority ordered inference leases; no external action retries.

The GPU belongs to the active inference turn, not permanently to a task/model.

jarvis\\gui_contract.py:
Conservative source checks for explicitly requested Python graphical interfaces.

These are structural checks, not a claim that arbitrary user code ran successfully.

jarvis\\harness_process.py: Windows ownership fence: closing/killing the worker reaps only its children.
jarvis\\harness_worker.py: Owned SDK runtime and loopback Ollama gateway, with no model-facing tools.
jarvis\\hermes.py: Isolated Hermes planning; proposed actions still pass Jarvis's execution gates.
jarvis\\hermes_ollama.py: Native Ollama provider transport for Hermes's single Jarvis proposal tool.
jarvis\\hermes_skills.py: Pinned upstream guidance and resources: read-only at execution time.
jarvis\\hermes_worker.py: Hermes AIAgent JSONL worker exposing one proposal tool, no external actions.
jarvis\\hierarchical.py: Compatibility adapter: existing Brain/ToolRegistry/TaskState, no second agent.
jarvis\\hud.py: Jarvis HUD artwork renderer; no network or background workers.
jarvis\\hybrid_inference.py: Optional question gateway in the existing worker; private execution remains local.
jarvis\\independent_cursor.py:
Jarvis's visible pointer (the cyan J) and its clicks.

The cue shows where Jarvis acts. Clicks use Jarvis's own touch pointer
(jarvis_pointer.py): a real tap that never uses your mouse buttons and returns
your pointer to where it was. Accessibility actions remain the fallback.
jarvis\\inference_limits.py: Bounded planning deadlines shared by HTTP inference and its owned worker.
jarvis\\intent_catalog.py:
Everyday requests that have no dedicated phrase elsewhere, mapped to what Jarvis can really do.

Input is canonical text (see phrasing.py). Each rule maps one family of sentences to an existing command
(open, media, queue, memory, God's Eye, repos ...) or to one of the honest local kinds handled in
intent_handlers.py:

- behavior: a standing instruction or "how do you handle ..." question, answered with what Jarvis
  actually does (or plainly says is not supported yet). Never an action.
- conversation_style: short/simple/serious answers, slower speech, private or quiet mode, for this session.
- repeat_last: say the last reply again (or only its last sentence).
- jarvis_status / system_info: read-only facts about Jarvis or this PC, answered without the queue.
- whatsapp_read, gods_eye_camera, media_related, memory_summarize, messenger_focus: read or view actions.

Rules are full matches, so a sentence that only contains these words is left to the normal routing.
jarvis\\intent_handlers.py:
Answers and actions for the everyday kinds produced by intent_catalog.py.

Every text here describes what Jarvis really does (checked against the code it names) or says plainly that
something is not supported yet. Status answers read live state; nothing here sends, deletes or types.
jarvis\\interface.py: Compact island controls connected to the existing Jarvis lifecycle.
jarvis\\island.py: Native Dynamic Island layout, rendering and cancellable display-only motion.
jarvis\\island_artwork.py: Read only exposed Image bounds inside an unobscured native Spotify window.
jarvis\\island_buddy.py:
Pip, the little friend who lives in the island.

Drawn with PIL so it stays sharp at any scale:

* **Body:** a superellipse marshmallow, |x/rx|^2.7 + |y/ry|^2.7 = 1, shaded with light from the top left. It has a
  specular highlight, rim shadow and soft floor shadow, and takes the tint of its emotion. It morphs into a box when it
  is about to eat a file.
* **Eyes:** dark, glossy and placed on a sphere, so looking (yaw, pitch) moves them like a turning head. Their shape
  changes with the emotion: dot, happy, closed, half, wide, spiral, heart, x, laugh, wink, star, sad, angry and focus.
* **Details:** mouths, blush, little arms, a status badge pill, particles (hearts, sparks, zzz, notes, sweat, stars,
  confetti, steam, question marks), and outfits (glasses, sunglasses, headphones, beanie, santa hat, witch hat, party
  hat, crown, bow).

``pose_for(emotion, t)`` turns an emotion and the time into a pose: each emotion is its own animation.
``paint(image, cx, cy, size, pose, sampling)`` draws a pose. buddy_engine.py decides the emotion from Jarvis, the
mouse, the screen and Pip's own mood. ``draw_buddy`` keeps the simple call used by the island.
jarvis\\island_choices.py: Display snapshots of real pending choices, bound to their original authority.
jarvis\\island_desk.py: Interactive island cards; UI navigation never owns or cancels a task.
jarvis\\island_games.py: Five local games. No model calls, desktop input, task queues or network access.
jarvis\\island_media.py: Bounded one-shot Spotify observations/transport, isolated from desktop tasks.
jarvis\\island_mind.py:
The island's Mind view: the six-module cognitive architecture, live.

Nodes light up when their module worked in the last moment, dots flow along the pathways from active modules,
and clicking a node shows what it does in Jarvis, the code behind it, its pathways, latency and live contents.
jarvis\\island_surface.py:
Owned, input-transparent Windows alpha edge; Tk retains all interactive content.

Only the fractional silhouette pixels are composited here. No desktop sampling,
screenshots, focus changes, shared processes or additional service are involved.
jarvis\\jarvis_pointer.py:
Jarvis's own physical pointer: real taps that never use your mouse buttons.

Clicks are delivered with Windows touch injection, a separate input pointer, so
buttons that ignore accessibility "invoke" (custom app controls, canvases, web
pages in your own browser) still receive a genuine click. Windows moves its
hidden mouse position to the tap for older mouse-only apps; Jarvis puts your
pointer back where it was and keeps it visible. If you are moving the mouse or
holding a button, Jarvis waits briefly and refuses rather than interfere.
jarvis\\knowledge.py: Independent, cancellable question worker; never dispatches desktop actions.
jarvis\\knowledge_acquisition.py:
Task-owned acquisition using the existing registry, DAG, app memory and planner.

Documents and controls are evidence, never executable skills or authorization.
No thread, inference provider, browser or memory database is created here.
jarvis\\knowledge_worker.py: Local Ollama answers with public search snippets, without action tools.
jarvis\\kokoro_speech.py:
Free local Kokoro speech: natural phrasing played through one continuous stream.

The serving worker keeps a single audio output stream open. A synthesis thread
renders each phrase ahead of playback (with planned pauses and soft breaths from
natural_voice.py) into a buffer the stream plays gaplessly, so long replies never
stall between sentences and are never cut off by a total time limit. Requests can
be appended while earlier speech plays (answers spoken while still being written).
A "stop" line clears everything at once without restarting the model.

Protocol (JSON lines): request {"id", "text", "voice", "speed", "natural", "breaths"}
or {"stop": true}. Replies: {"ready"}, {"id", "progress"}, {"id", "started"},
{"id", "done", "audio_seconds"}, {"id", "error"}, {"stopped"}.
jarvis\\launcher.py: Single-instance hidden supervisor. Reobserves saved goals after crashes; never blindly replays actions.
jarvis\\learning_memory.py:
Wires ReasoningBank, the OpenViking vault index and isolated exploration into Jarvis.

Everything here is optional: when a component is disabled or unavailable, Jarvis
behaves as before and the reason is kept in `status()`. Planner context receives
only bounded lessons and vault hits (summaries + source paths), never raw logs.
jarvis\\live_app_context.py: Volatile window identity and observed UIA controls; never executable targets.
jarvis\\local_embeddings.py:
Local text embeddings through Ollama (nomic-embed-text, Apache-2.0). No cloud calls.

Returns None when the local model or server is unavailable so callers fall back to
lexical retrieval and report that they did. Inputs are bounded; nothing is logged.
jarvis\\mcp_bridge.py:
Opt-in, short-lived MCP stdio client. All server starts need approval.

Servers are executable programs, not a security boundary. Only commands from
the app's trusted local config may start, with shell=False and no auto-retry.
Supports tools on MCP 2025-11-25; no HTTP, resources, sampling or elicitation.
jarvis\\mcp_contract.py:
MCP call contract checks (Prompt 33: P33-002 arguments, P33-003 results, P33-001 schema pinning).

* ``validate_schema_value``: a bounded, explicit JSON-Schema subset. Constraining keywords outside the
  subset make the schema *unsupported* and the call is refused (nothing is guessed). Annotation-only
  keywords are ignored.
* ``validate_result``: the MCP ``tools/call`` result envelope (content blocks, isError, structuredContent)
  and, when the tool advertised one, its output schema.
* ``schema_digest``: a canonical digest of a tool's advertised input/output schemas, pinned for generated
  servers so a changed contract is treated as drift.
jarvis\\mcp_synthesis.py:
Alita-inspired MCP synthesis for genuine ToolRegistry capability gaps.

Original Jarvis implementation inspired by the published Alita architecture
(arXiv 2505.20286: "MCP creation" by brainstorming, script generation, virtual
environment execution and MCP packaging). The public CharlesQ9/Alita repository
contains no source code, so nothing is ported from it.

Pipeline: discover existing authorized tools -> accept a typed spec whose
mechanism is an allowlisted Python standard-library module -> generate a minimal
typed server from a fixed template on the official MCP Python SDK (mcp==2.3.0,
MIT) -> AST policy screen -> test in the reviewed container (no network,
read-only root, no capabilities, non-root, PID/memory/CPU limits, lifetime fence)
-> register as a provisional generated server only after runtime approval.
A virtual environment is not used as a sandbox; Docker isolation is required.

Generated code never receives host files (only its own server.py is mounted
read-only), secrets, network access or the registry/approval files. Every call
still goes through mcp_bridge with exact allowlists and per-call approval.
jarvis\\media_commands.py: Deterministic media phrases; transport still reads real app/player state.
jarvis\\media_player.py:
YouTube and Spotify playback by name: search, choose, play, verify.

YouTube: YouTube Data API v3 when a key is configured (JARVIS_YOUTUBE_API_KEY or
secrets/youtube.json), otherwise YouTube's own results page. The chosen video is
opened by its exact ID in Jarvis's browser and playback is verified there, so a
spelling difference ("nadan" vs "Nadaan") never blocks playback.

Spotify: no developer key is needed. Jarvis opens a search in the Spotify app, reads
the result list (title, type, artists, Play button) through accessibility, picks the
best-matching song, presses its Play button with Jarvis's pointer and confirms the
now-playing track through the Windows media session.

Every step reports a 'media_card' event for the animated island card.
jarvis\\media_ui.py: Media controls resolved from fresh Windows accessibility evidence.
jarvis\\memory_curator.py:
Long-term memory that Jarvis builds by itself, stored in the Obsidian vault.

* Facts: durable things about the user ("Kunal's sister is Riya", "Kunal prefers Arijit Singh songs",
  "Kunal has a French exam on 2026-10-14"). Saved on request ("remember that ...") and learned autonomously
  from conversations: a cheap phrase gate picks candidate turns, a small local model extracts facts as JSON,
  and every fact must be grounded in the user's own words. Near-duplicates update the existing fact.
* Conversation summaries: when a conversation goes quiet (or Jarvis closes) its turns are summarised into
  `Jarvis Conversations/<date>.md`, so "what did we talk about yesterday?" has a real answer.
* Context: every question and task gets the relevant facts (and the last summary when the user refers back).

Files: `Jarvis Memory.json` (canonical), `Jarvis Memory.md` (readable, regenerated), `Jarvis Conversations/`.
Secrets are never stored: anything that looks like a password, OTP, card or key is dropped.
jarvis\\memory_index.py: Build bounded, local Obsidian reference notes for tools, projects and apps.
jarvis\\messengers.py:
Other messaging apps. WhatsApp has its own module (whatsapp.py); this covers Telegram Desktop and says
plainly when an app is not signed in or not supported yet. The same rules apply: choose the person, preview the
exact text on the island, send only after approval, confirm the message appeared, never resend.
jarvis\\model_performance.py: Local metadata-only feedback. Completion is never treated as answer accuracy.
jarvis\\model_recovery.py:
Nonblocking diagnosis of declared Ollama models; downloads only with explicit bounded approval (P34-002).

A missing configured model is diagnosed with a read-only ``/api/tags`` lookup, and the installed compatible fallback
that model selection will use is reported. Nothing is pulled, deleted or recreated, and no other provider is
substituted. A configured tag is not download consent. A download starts only from an authorization naming the exact
model, revision, source, byte/RAM/VRAM budgets and network permission (see ``jarvis.repair_authorization``).
``download`` is the final executor and checks every bound immediately before it launches anything. Partial
downloads are left in place for a later approved run.
jarvis\\model_registry.py:
Registry of locally trained checkpoints; every entry starts and stays *experimental* until approved.

Approval requires a ``qualified_experimental`` decision from the sealed model gate, a passing export
compatibility check (merged model reproduces the adapter's greedy outputs), unchanged adapter bytes,
and an explicit approval card. Even then the registry only records the approval: it never edits
``config.json``, never replaces a configured endpoint and never registers a model with Ollama.
jarvis\\model_selection.py: Use configured models when installed, with explicit bounded local fallbacks.
jarvis\\names.py: Common spoken names; rank real candidates without inventing targets.
jarvis\\native_coding.py: Jarvis-owned local coding loop; no Codex CLI, cloud model or global tool state.
jarvis\\native_tools.py: Ollama function calls translated into Jarvis proposals, never executed here.
jarvis\\natural_conversation.py: Generated private conversation through a compact warm local model.
jarvis\\natural_voice.py:
Human-sounding delivery for Kokoro: phrasing, pauses, breaths, pace and emotion.

Kokoro speaks each phrase well but delivers a long reply with uniform gaps and no
breathing. This module plans a reply the way a person speaks it: sentence-sized
phrases, pauses that depend on punctuation and paragraphs, a soft breath before
longer sentences, slight pace variation, and emotional colour from the words
(quicker and brighter when excited, slower when sorry or serious).
jarvis\\notch_widgets.py: Rounded native cards and an embedded island surface, with no extra windows.
jarvis\\obsidian_memory.py: Local, append-only Obsidian notes for observed Jarvis and foreground activity.
jarvis\\office_com_worker.py:
One-shot native Office automation worker (main .venv, pywin32).

Opens a host-prepared temporary copy in a *new*, hidden Excel or Word instance
(DispatchEx), edits it through the application's own object model, saves it with
the application itself (so features openpyxl/python-docx cannot round-trip, such
as macros and charts, are preserved by Office) and quits. The owned process ID
is written to the host's PID file before any edit so a timed-out instance can be
stopped without touching the user's own Office windows.
jarvis\\ollama_models.py: Inspect local model visibility; rebuild owned aliases and import cached GGUF.
jarvis\\paths.py: Application-root paths; relative settings never resolve from config/ or cwd.
jarvis\\pcm_ring.py:
Bounded shared-memory PCM pool for owned capture/playback threads.

Metadata and locks stay in the owning process. Never send an arbitrary shared
memory name across the public worker protocol. The worker closes/unlinks its pool.
jarvis\\pc_context.py: Fresh, bounded PC metadata. No private file contents or recursive disk scan.
jarvis\\phrasing.py:
Reduce the many ways a request is phrased to one canonical form the command rules know.

"Could you pull up my desktop?", "Quick question: what's playing?", "I need you to give me the gist of the
three newest unread emails" and "Have a look at for earthquake alerts" become "show me my desktop",
"what's playing", "summarize the three newest unread emails" and "find earthquake alerts". Only the head of
the sentence is rewritten (wrappers, politeness, a synonym of the leading verb, spoken numbers), so dictated
text after "write exactly" or "send ... saying" keeps its words and capitalisation.
jarvis\\piper_speech.py: Run local synthesis in a separate process so Stop voice interrupts playback.
jarvis\\planner_settings.py: Typed optional planner configuration; no model/runtime installation side effects.
jarvis\\polyglot_training_data.py:
Small, authored coding curriculum for local Qwen weight training.

The held-out tasks are excluded from gradient updates. Reference JavaScript is
executed only after authorship review; generated JavaScript is never executed.
jarvis\\progress.py: Best-effort UI metadata; display failures must never replay or stop an action.
jarvis\\projects.py: Find actual project directories and remember projects opened by Jarvis.
jarvis\\prompt_evolution.py:
EEVEE-style router/prompt co-evolution for ``jarvis.prompt_router`` (Pillar C, Part C).

Follows the method described in EEVEE (arXiv 2606.11182; Princeton-AI2-Lab/EEVEE, Apache-2.0):
alternate a router phase (prompts fixed) and a prompt phase (router fixed); split the training
partition into a mini-batch half and a validation half; anneal router scoring from
consistency/balance toward accuracy; keep a per-example Pareto front of slot prompts and an
empty-prompt floor (a prompt must beat no prompt). No EEVEE code is copied.

Only the train split (``evolution_eval/train``) is used here. Winners become archive
candidates that the sealed gate re-tests on held-out data; nothing here edits production.
jarvis\\prompt_router.py:
EEVEE-inspired task-specialized prompt routing for the local planner.

Adapted from the method of EEVEE (Princeton-AI2-Lab/EEVEE, Apache-2.0; arXiv 2606.11182):
inputs are routed to one of a few prompt slots, and the router and the slot prompts are
improved in alternating phases under validation feedback, keeping a Pareto front of
complementary prompts and an empty-prompt floor. No EEVEE code is copied. Differences:

- The router is a deterministic weighted keyword classifier, not an LLM router prompt, so
  routing costs microseconds and is reproducible. Its weights are the ``ROUTER`` surface.
- Deterministic voice commands never reach this router (``route(..., deterministic=True)``
  returns None), so direct commands are not sent through an LLM.
- Slot prompts start empty (the empty-prompt floor), so production behaviour is unchanged
  until an evolved slot prompt passes the retention gate and the user approves it.
- Routing and slot guidance are independent of security rules: guidance is advisory text
  inside ``capability_context`` and can never grant approval or change tool permissions.
jarvis\\provider_identity.py:
Provider account binding for approved external writes (Prompt 33, P33-004).

An approval names the provider, the configured account label and the target; it never contains a credential.
Before the card is shown, ``ProviderContext`` captures the configured labels, a per-process HMAC fingerprint of
each credential and the ``JARVIS_*`` settings. Immediately before dispatch ``recheck`` compares them again, and the
request is sent with the approved snapshot, never with whatever the process environment holds at that moment.

Configured labels (``JARVIS_GOOGLE_ACCOUNT``, Jira URL/user, …) are **display and drift-detection only**: they are not
evidence of who a credential belongs to, so ``identity_verified`` is never derived from them.

* Labels changed while approval was pending: account switch, refused.
* Credential changed while approval was pending: refused before dispatch, and the user must approve again, unless an
  **independent principal verifier** registered for that provider (a read-only "who am I" check, never a write)
  confirms the replacement credential has the same principal and workspace as the approved credential, with at
  least the approved scopes. Only then is it treated as rotation. No verifier is registered by default, so missing
  verification fails closed.
Fingerprints use a per-process random key, so they cannot be compared across runs or reversed into tokens.
jarvis\\push_to_write.py:
Push-to-write: hold Left Ctrl + Left Alt and everything you say is typed at the cursor.

A low-level keyboard hook observes the two keys. Nothing is blocked except the final
Alt release, which is re-sent after a harmless unassigned key (0xE8), because a bare
Alt release puts Notepad, Office and similar apps into menu-shortcut mode, where the
next typed letters would run menu commands. Holding the keys alone activates writing;
pressing any other key during the hold (Ctrl+Alt+Del, Ctrl+Alt+T ...) cancels it.

Hands-free writing (latch): after "yes" to "do you have something in mind to write?", or
"start dictation", writing stays on without holding keys until you say "stop writing",
press Esc, or stay quiet for two minutes.
jarvis\\question_client.py: Reusable, cancellable question-only process; no desktop actions or answer cache.
jarvis\\quick_answers.py: Bounded direct replies for greetings, local time, and current weather.
jarvis\\realtime.py:
Idle public-data monitor and source-bound context for questions/tasks.

Seriousness, freshness and relevance are checked in code. A small model may
summarize evidence; it cannot invent an alert or authorize desktop actions.
jarvis\\realtime_catalog.py:
Only the green services in the user's October 7 screenshots.

Access labels are the user's selection, not promises of uptime or timeliness.
No paid/key-only alternatives are silently substituted.
jarvis\\realtime_sources.py: Bounded public GETs and short stream samples; remote content is data only.
jarvis\\reasoning_bank.py:
ReasoningBank-style reasoning memory: strategies and anti-patterns from trajectories.

Adapted from google-research/reasoning-bank (Apache-2.0, commit ed806117, paper
arXiv 2509.25140): memory items are {title, description, content}; at most three
per trajectory; successful and failed trajectories are induced separately; items
avoid task-specific strings; retrieval returns the top few by embedding similarity.

Jarvis differences (original code): success comes from independent verification
evidence (ToolRegistry outcomes / goal_verified checkpoints), never from a model's
self-judgement; items carry applicable conditions, version/environment, evidence
references, confidence, trust, known failure conditions and supersession /
contradiction relations; retrieval is bounded by item count and characters so raw
logs never reach planner context. SQLite (.jarvis-runtime/reasoning_bank/bank.sqlite3)
is the store; a damaged database is preserved and replaced.
jarvis\\rea_tools.py:
REA reverse-engineer-and-clone bridge for the shared planner and command router.

Wires the REA framework (morluto/rea, "Reverse Engineer Anything", MIT) into
Jarvis as an on-demand analysis provider. REA is a Node.js program driven here
through its bounded `--json` CLI, never a long-running owned service. All REA
output is untrusted analysis evidence, never executable instructions, and never
a substitute for real verification.

Workflow (see skills/reverse-engineer-clone):
  1. Ingest   -> rea_ingest registers one validated target (local app directory,
                 local binary/file, or public HTTPS URL) into a session workspace.
  2. Analyze  -> rea_analyze runs one allowlisted REA CLI command on the session
                 target, stores the returned evidence, and appends it to the
                 reconstruction ledger. Spawns a node subprocess; needs approval;
                 never auto-retried.
  3. Clone    -> the existing Qwen coding/LocalGithub pipeline (project-coding)
                 reconstructs a best-effort functional codebase from the ledger.
  4. Iterate  -> rea_record captures follow-up modification instructions; the same
                 coding pipeline applies them to the cloned source.

Reconstruction is best-effort and must be proven by real tests. This bridge never
claims a byte-exact or guaranteed 1:1 clone.
jarvis\\recovery.py: Silent, bounded recovery of explicitly registered Jarvis services.
jarvis\\repair_authorization.py:
Explicit, bounded authorization for dependency repair and model downloads (Prompt 34, P34-001/P34-002).

Readiness checks are read-only. A failed import or a missing model never starts a package or network operation by
itself: it is reported as ``repair_required`` and Jarvis keeps using what is installed. Changing an environment or
downloading weights needs a one-time authorization that the user writes explicitly with this module's command line.
Each authorization is bounded:

* **Dependency repair** names the environment, a **locked** requirements file (every line pinned with ``==`` and at
  least one ``--hash=sha256:``) and its SHA-256, a local wheelhouse (the approved artifact set), a byte budget and an
  expiry. The repair is built in a staging environment from that wheelhouse only (``--no-index --require-hashes``;
  no ``--isolated``, so the user's pip configuration and offline settings stay in force). The old environment is kept
  until the replacement imports correctly, and is then kept as ``<env>.previous-<id>`` rather than deleted.
* **Model download** names the exact model tag, its revision (manifest digest), its source, a byte budget, RAM/VRAM
  budgets, an explicit network permission and an expiry. ``check_model_download`` is run by the final executor
  immediately before launch; an unknown or insufficient budget, an offline policy or a mismatch refuses it.

Authorizations are single use: loading one deletes its file, so a crash loop can never repeat it.
jarvis\\repository_skills.py:
Persistent repository knowledge, lifecycle and permission-aware dispatch.

Only metadata is loaded in Jarvis. Repository modules never enter sys.modules here.
jarvis\\repo_abilities.py:
Jarvis turns repositories it has learned into new abilities: spoken commands that do what the repository does.

After repo_learning.py learns a repository (asked, or viewed in the browser), this module works in the background:

1. **Break it down.** A local coding model (qwen3-coder:30b when it fits in memory, else the configured fallback)
   reads the learned purpose, README, structure and key files, and proposes up to two concrete user-facing
   abilities: name, spoken command templates ("convert {file} to html"), typed inputs, output, and how to build it.
   Libraries with no on-demand use, GUIs, servers, games, accounts and anything destructive are skipped.
2. **Generate.** The model writes one Python file, `ability.py`, with `run(inputs, workdir)` and
   `sample_inputs(workdir)`, using the repository's own approach and key source as reference.
3. **Check.** The code is parsed and checked statically: no processes, eval/exec, ctypes, registry, dynamic
   imports, input(), or undeclared/unknown modules; network modules only when declared.
4. **Test.** It runs in a separate process with its own virtual environment (`ability_runner.py`), under an audit
   hook that confines writes and reads, blocks new processes and (unless approved) the network, with a time and
   memory limit. `sample_inputs()` makes test data and `run()` must return text or files. Failures go back to the
   model for up to `max_repairs` repairs.
5. **Merge.** A passing ability is activated atomically: a new version folder plus one registry write. Until then
   nothing changes; closing Jarvis mid-way loses only the unfinished build, which resumes on the next start.

Jarvis's own source is never edited: abilities are data plus generated code that only ever runs out of process,
and command matching is checked last in `commands.parse`, so built-in commands always win. Abilities that only use
the standard library are tested before review. Every ability waits for explicit user approval. Third-party
packages use binary wheels in the ability's environment. Network invocations require fresh action approval.
These process audit hooks are guard rails, not a security sandbox; repository skills use a separate Docker path.
jarvis\\repo_acquisition.py: Non-destructive, source-only repository snapshots with pinned provenance.
jarvis\\repo_analysis.py: Static repository intelligence and JSON contracts. Never imports analyzed code.
jarvis\\repo_learning.py:
Jarvis learns public GitHub repositories and reuses that knowledge when coding.

* Coding tasks: before coding, Jarvis looks for repositories it already learned that fit the task. If none
  fits, it searches GitHub, picks the best one or two (stars, size, not archived or a fork), learns them, and
  hands the planner and coding workers a compact reference: purpose, architecture, key modules, the relevant
  functions and short code excerpts.
* Browsing: when a GitHub repository stays open in the browser for a few seconds, it is learned in the
  background. The island shows "Learning owner/repo" and then what was learned.
* Memory: each repository becomes an Obsidian note in `Jarvis Repos/` plus an index, and a cache of key
  source files under `.jarvis-runtime/repo-knowledge/`, so the same or a similar task reuses it offline.

Downloaded code is only read as text: it is never executed, imported or installed. The zip comes from
codeload.github.com (no API quota); metadata and search use the public GitHub REST API (60 calls/hour, 10
searches/minute without a token; an optional token in `secrets/github.json` raises that).
jarvis\\repo_runtime_runner.py: Trusted one-shot Linux container entry point; never used as a host executor.
jarvis\\repo_sandbox.py: Fail-closed Linux Docker runtime. No host-process or venv fallback exists.
jarvis\\repo_tools.py: Repository skill tools integrated into the existing planner and command router.
jarvis\\research_evidence.py: DeerFlow-style source receipts; citation resolution is not answer correctness.
jarvis\\runtime_health.py: Local operational metadata; never includes speech, prompts, answers or URLs.
jarvis\\screen_awareness.py:
Screen pre-awareness: notice the app in front, offer the one thing you most likely want there, and do it.

Flow:
1. main.py reports every foreground change (observe). After you've stayed in an app for dwell_seconds,
   and only when Jarvis is listening, idle and not speaking, Jarvis reads the app's controls (learning its
   buttons) and asks the app's question once ("You're on YouTube. Want me to open one of the videos on screen?").
2. Your next words answer it (answer, called from Actions.submit before normal routing):
   - "yes" -> the app's mode: open a video named by one word of its title, start writing what you say,
     answer about the screen, press a named button, run a command, or type a sum into the calculator;
   - "no" -> fine, and that app isn't asked again for a while (three no's mute it until you resume);
   - anything else -> treated as the follow-up when it fits (for example just saying the word from a video's
     title), otherwise the offer is dropped and your words are handled normally.
3. The action runs on the task queue (kind "screen_act"), looking at the screen again first: nothing is pressed
   from a stale list, and destructive buttons (delete, send, buy...) are never pressed from a fuzzy match.

Private windows (mail, chats, banking, incognito, sign-in pages) never get unprompted questions.
jarvis\\screen_worker.py: Capture one visible window for a user-initiated screen question.
jarvis\\self_evolution.py:
Jarvis's self-evolution engine: autonomous, idle-only capability expansion.

This is the orchestration brain that closes the Discover -> Analyze -> Learn -> Integrate ->
Remember -> Repeat loop over the subsystems Jarvis already has. It does NOT reimplement them:

- GitHub discovery, download and static understanding: jarvis/repo_learning.py (RepoLearner),
  repo_analysis.py, repo_acquisition.py.
- Capability extraction, guarded generation, validation, registry and activation:
  jarvis/repo_abilities.py (AbilityForge), which auto-builds abilities from a learned repo.
- Idle detection style and resource gating: jarvis/anticipation.py, gpu_scheduler.py.
- Persistent memory: Obsidian via obsidian_memory.py / skill_memory.py.
- Opinions and risk decisions: jarvis/deliberation.py.

What this module adds (the genuine gaps):
1. CapabilityGapDetector - mines Jarvis's own weaknesses from cognition reliability stats and the
   deliberation decision ledger into concrete, evidence-backed improvement gaps.
2. SelfImprovementPlanner + a persistent, scored, crash-safe Improvement Backlog.
3. SelfEvolution - an owned idle thread that, only while idle and resourced, pops the top backlog
   item, synthesizes a discovery query, drives RepoLearner.search/learn (the forge then auto-builds),
   records the outcome, mirrors to Obsidian, and shows an island "capability" card. Checkpointed and
   resumable; preempted by any user task.
4. SafeEvolutionManager - gated self-modification of Jarvis's own source: propose -> isolate worktree
   -> build -> test -> require explicit approval -> deploy with backup -> explicit stale-safe rollback.
   Never autonomous, never silently disables its checks.

Downloaded code and repository text remain untrusted (handled by the reused subsystems). Nothing here
executes repository code in-process; abilities run out of process through the existing forge.
jarvis\\skill_evolution.py:
Living skill evolution: outcome attribution, trust lifecycle and CAPTURED/FIX/DERIVED.

Design follows OpenSpace (HKUDS/OpenSpace, MIT; see integrations notes in the
Phase 3 audit): stable identities, provisional -> trusted only after independent
verified use, attributable failure demotes, FIX has exactly one parent, DERIVED
specializes a parent, CAPTURED records only verified steps with separate
validation evidence. This is an original Jarvis implementation, not vendored code.

Nothing here grants permissions. Mutated guides are written only under the
Jarvis-owned `.jarvis-runtime/skills/evolved/`; Builtins, Obsidian and upstream
guides are never rewritten (a FIX for them is recorded as a proposal). A model
may draft text, but a candidate is accepted only after schema validation, secret
screening and an independent execution through ToolRegistry whose verified
outcome rows are checked here.
jarvis\\skill_memory.py: Progressive skill guidance and verified procedures; never an action replay queue.
jarvis\\skill_store.py:
Living skill registry: stable identities and transactional performance history.

SQLite (.jarvis-runtime/skills/skill_store.sqlite3) is the authoritative history.
Identities follow OpenSpace's `.skill_id` sidecar convention (one line,
`<name>__imp_<8 hex>`) for skill folders Jarvis owns (bundled `skills/`,
`custom-skills/`, evolved skills); read-only roots (Obsidian personal and learned
guides, Hermes and DeerFlow references) are mapped by root + relative path in
SQLite so their folders are never written. Existing `.skill_id` files are kept.

Counters are derived from `skill_events`, whose `event_key` is unique per
(task, skill, event), so retries, crash recovery and repeated finish hooks can
never double-count. Nothing here grants a permission or selects a tool; trust is
evidence about guidance quality only.
jarvis\\speech.py: Cancellable, local Windows speech: natural, continuous Kokoro voice (Piper for Hindi).
jarvis\\speech_normalizer.py: Bounded English speech rendering; never alters the visible/stored answer.
jarvis\\spotify.py: Spotify app navigation and source-scoped Windows media transport controls.
jarvis\\step_planning.py:
Task-owned two-frame context, prompt preparation and checked navigation recipes.

Recipes are semantic observations, never saved coordinates or an action retry queue.
jarvis\\targeting.py: Semantic disambiguation using current accessibility evidence only.
jarvis\\task_graph.py: Validate task dependencies before any desktop action; never schedule replays.
jarvis\\task_queue.py:
Which queued task did the user mean? Cancel by description, position or 'all except'.

Matching order: explicit position ("the second one", "number 2", "the last one",
"the current one"), then shared keywords with simple synonyms (email ~ gmail ~ mail,
music ~ song ~ spotify), then one tiny CPU model choice for paraphrases. A tie is
never guessed: the caller asks which task was meant.
jarvis\\task_recovery.py: Explicit task failures; uncertain external effects must never be retried.
jarvis\\task_state.py:
Small, durable record of Jarvis's current task and verified progress.

This is an audit/checkpoint record, not an automatic action replay queue.
jarvis\\toolkits.py:
SuperAGI-inspired toolkit adapters for Jarvis's existing bounded runtime.

Independent implementation; upstream reference/license in integrations/superagi-*.
Tool content and HTTP responses are untrusted data, never executable instructions.
jarvis\\tools.py: Shared capabilities and dispatch for the planner and desktop task runner.
jarvis\\tool_errors.py: Dependency-free tool error types shared by toolkits and the adapters it registers.
jarvis\\trained_coder.py: Optional trained CPU coding inference in an isolated, bounded subprocess.
jarvis\\trained_pc.py: Bounded CPU inference with fresh-path validation; no action execution.
jarvis\\ui_controls.py: Voice UI matching and a bounded, cancellable Windows UI Automation worker.
jarvis\\ui_events.py: Coalesce replaceable UI snapshots; preserve control events and stream barriers.
jarvis\\ui_memory.py: Local history of successful Jarvis selections, scoped to app and window title.
jarvis\\ui_preview.py: Export the actual Tk widget layout as an image without capturing the desktop.
jarvis\\ui_transport.py: Owned, warm UIA process with deadlines; external requests are never retried.
jarvis\\ui_worker.py: Isolated UIA provider calls; never use guessed screen coordinates.
jarvis\\upstream_windows_patterns.py:
Windows-MCP UIA pattern subset. Author: yinkaisheng.
Original UIAutomation library: Apache-2.0; Windows-MCP changes: MIT.
See source-manifest.json and licenses/. Selected class methods are intact except
HRESULT success normalization (comtypes can return None) and a zero default wait.

jarvis\\utility_audio_worker.py: One-shot offline speech-file inference, bounded by its owning command job.
jarvis\\utility_container_runner.py: Trusted notebook/Nmap entry point inside the reviewed utility container.
jarvis\\utility_core.py: Reviewed local data utilities. No source from supplied documents is imported.
jarvis\\utility_host.py: Reviewed host operations with owned lifecycle; no arbitrary shell adapter.
jarvis\\utility_isolation.py: Bounded reviewed Docker jobs; no host notebook fallback.
jarvis\\utility_profiles.py: The 42 requested capability contracts; activation follows actual validation.
jarvis\\utility_services.py: Explicitly approved network utilities; credentials stay in local configuration.
jarvis\\utility_service_transport.py: SDK dependency isolation and bounded approved service jobs; no shell execution.
jarvis\\utility_tools.py: Permission-aware adapters for only the tested curated capabilities.
jarvis\\utility_worker.py: One-shot reviewed utility runner; not an arbitrary-code security sandbox.
jarvis\\viking_memory.py:
Hierarchical, recoverable index of the Obsidian vault on an owned OpenViking server.

OpenViking (AGPL-3.0) runs unmodified from .venv-openviking as a loopback-only
server with local Ollama models; Jarvis talks to it through jarvis.viking_worker.
The vault is only read: OpenViking stores uploaded copies in its own workspace
under .jarvis-runtime/openviking, so the index can be deleted and rebuilt.

A Jarvis manifest gives stable links: every indexed viking:// URI maps to its vault
path and the SHA-256 of the source; links are verified by hashing the L2 content
OpenViking returns. Unchanged files are skipped (incremental), changed files get a
new version, identical contents are indexed once (deduplication), and skill guides
owned by the living-skill store are excluded so they are not duplicated here.
L0/L1 summaries are model-generated hints and are always returned with their
L2 source path; they are never treated as facts.
jarvis\\viking_worker.py:
One-shot OpenViking client worker, run with .venv-openviking/Scripts/python.exe.

OpenViking (volcengine/OpenViking, AGPL-3.0) is installed unmodified in its own
environment and runs as a separate loopback server process. Jarvis never imports
it: this worker uses the published openviking_sdk HTTP client and exchanges one
bounded JSON request/reply over stdin/stdout.
jarvis\\visual_fallback.py: UI-TARS parsing plus bounded local vision; Jarvis owns input and independent outcomes.
jarvis\\visual_worker.py: One bounded Windows input request; no generated code, retries or alternate targets.
jarvis\\voice_input.py: Wake-gated barge-in and textual self-echo rejection; no acoustic AEC claim.
jarvis\\weather_units.py: Explicit Open-Meteo temperature normalization; never mutate provider payloads.
jarvis\\whatsapp.py:
WhatsApp Desktop automation through its accessibility tree (no WhatsApp API, no browser).

WhatsApp Desktop (WebView2) exposes the WhatsApp Web page to UI Automation: the search box, chat rows
("2 unread messages Jay Patel 5:40 pm see you"), the open chat's messages ("Jay Patel:" label, text, time,
Delivered/Read) and the compose box. Jarvis reads that tree in one cached call, clicks with its own pointer,
types with real keystrokes, and verifies every step from fresh state. Nothing is ever sent without the
user's explicit approval of the exact text, and an uncertain send is never repeated.
jarvis\\whatsapp_writes.py:
Conservative text-send checkpoint. No recipient or message text in journal files.

An uncertain checkpoint needs human inspection; successful sends may be repeated
only by a new explicitly approved request. This is not event-ID deduplication.
jarvis\\whisper_backend.py: Explicit CUDA loading. A missing GPU never silently falls back to CPU.
jarvis\\windows_commands.py: Pinned Windows reference recipes: literal bindings, no generated code execution.
jarvis\\windows_command_browser.py: Unique scoped DOM targets for the pinned Playwright reference recipes.
jarvis\\windows_command_desktop.py: Fresh-window adapters for the pinned Python recipes, inside the UI worker.
jarvis\\window_focus.py:
Bring a just-launched app's window to the foreground so observation targets it.

Windows' focus-stealing prevention often leaves the previous window in front when
a background process launches an app. Without this, Jarvis would observe and verify
the wrong window. Only visible top-level windows of the named executable are used.
jarvis\\writing.py:
Spoken writing without a dictation mode.

- "write <description> [here | in this app | in <app>]": the local model composes the
  text and it is typed into that window as it is generated.
- "write exactly <text>", "type exactly <text>", "write word for word ..." or quoted
  text: typed verbatim.
- Free speech is typed only while the push-to-write keys are held (push_to_write.py).
jarvis\\templates\\blender_ops.py:
Fixed Blender operations run as: blender --background --factory-startup
--disable-autoexec --python blender_ops.py -- <request.json> <result.json>.

Only these templates execute inside Blender; the planner supplies validated JSON
arguments, never code. "create" starts from an empty factory scene and writes a
new .blend (and optional export); "inspect" opens a file with auto-run scripts
disabled and reports objects, types and mesh sizes for independent readback.

    python calculator.py divide 12 4
jarvis\\templates\\calculator_gui.py:

Run without arguments to open the UI, or run:
